title: General-state Markov kernels, invariance, and reversibility

items.title: General-state reversibility by symmetric flow measure
items.statement: On an arbitrary measurable state space, define the joint flow measure Lambda(dx,dy)=pi(dx)P(x,dy) for a probability measure pi and probability kernel P; call P reversible with respect to pi exactly when this measure is invariant under coordinate swap, without requiring a density or assuming pi is invariant in advance.
items.strategy: Use the probability-kernel joint-law theorem to define Lambda on the product sigma-algebra, define its transpose by the measurable coordinate-swap map, and state reversibility as equality of these two probability measures.

items.title: General-state reversibility implies invariance
items.statement: For any measurable state space, probability kernel P, and probability measure pi, symmetry of Lambda(dx,dy)=pi(dx)P(x,dy) implies pi P=pi on every measurable set.
items.strategy: Apply the kernel joint-law/Tonelli identity to the nonnegative indicator of X×A; symmetry swaps X×A and A×X, and the probability-kernel row mass makes the latter marginal equal pi(A).

title: General-state Markov kernels, invariance, and reversibility — Examples

items.title: A finite reversible two-state Markov kernel
items.statement: For 0<a,b≤1, the transition matrix [[1−a,a],[b,1−b]] is reversible with respect to pi=(b/(a+b),a/(a+b)) and therefore has that invariant probability.
items.strategy: Check the row sums and normalization, compare all four joint-flow atom masses under coordinate swap, and apply the general-state detailed-balance implication.

items.title: A symmetric random walk on the circle
items.statement: On the circle T=R/Z with normalized Haar probability m, the kernel P(x,A)=1/2 1_A(x+h)+1/2 1_A(x−h), for fixed 0<h<1/2, is reversible and invariant with respect to m; this remains a measure-level argument for its atomic transition law.
items.strategy: Use countable choice only through the existing normalized-circle-measure interface, verify the pointwise probability-kernel conditions, express the joint flow on product-measurable sets, and use translation invariance to show its coordinate transpose has the same measure.

items.title: A systematic composition of reversible kernels need not be reversible
items.statement: The chronological composition of two kernels that are each reversible for the same probability can preserve that probability without being reversible: two transposition updates on three states compose to a directed three-cycle.
items.strategy: Verify each deterministic transposition kernel has symmetric uniform flow, compute their chronological composition using the kernel-composition convention, and compare one off-diagonal atom with its transpose while checking the uniform invariant law directly.
